guard_streams.write_limit: ADR scheme process and KPI performance do not establish physical broadband availability, live orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the ADR performance page on 26 January 2024.
The page was last updated on 23 July 2026.
Ofcom reports KPIs for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
The KPI results are published quarterly.
Updated KPI thresholds apply from Q4 2025.
Communications Ombudsman answered 95% of calls within two minutes in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman reached 99% of case decisions within six weeks in Q2 2026.
CISAS answered 99% of calls within two minutes in Q2 2026.
CISAS reached 97% of case decisions within six weeks in Q2 2026.
Ofcom is the competent authority for communications and postal ADR bodies.

guard_streams.source: Making a complaint and using alternative dispute resolution (ADR) schemes
guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint escalation and redress rules are consumer-process evidence and cannot verify selected-parcel network coverage or performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the complaint and ADR guide on 8 March 2024.
The guide was last updated on 20 July 2026.
Customers should first contact their provider's customer services department.
If the issue remains unresolved, the customer should make a formal complaint.
Eligible customers can use an ADR scheme free of charge.
ADR schemes independently and impartially assess unresolved complaints.
Eligibility includes residential customers, small businesses and small not-for-profit organisations.
A complaint can be escalated after six weeks or after a deadlock letter.
Escalation must occur within 12 months of receiving a deadlock letter.
Ofcom currently approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman for telecom complaints.

guard_streams.write_limit: Market-wide portal data and sector commentary are aggregate context and do not prove serviceability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published The Communications Market 2026 on 30 June 2026.
The report is provided as an interactive data portal.
The portal includes data collected from industry by Ofcom.
It includes data from Ofcom consumer research.
It includes headline figures from selected third parties.
Related commentary is available in Media Nations.
Related commentary is available in Online Nation.
Related communications-infrastructure analysis is available in Connected Nations.
Ofcom published a short PDF summary of key findings.
The page provides a telecoms-data CSV download.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2026 interactive data page on 30 June 2026.
The page combines industry data, consumer research and selected third-party figures.
The interactive report includes a market-in-context section.
Market-in-context charts include communications affordability.
The report includes device and service take-up and use.
It includes a television and audiovisual section.
It includes a radio and audio section.
It includes a telecoms and networks section.
Telecoms charts include average monthly spend data.
Telecoms charts include home-broadband performance data.

guard_streams.write_limit: General regulatory conditions set provider obligations but do not establish current broadband orderability or speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the General Conditions page on 16 August 2023.
The page was last updated on 8 April 2026.
All providers of electronic communications networks and services must comply with applicable conditions.
The General Conditions replaced the former Telecommunications Act 1984 licensing regime.
The replacement took effect with the Communications Act 2003 framework.
The conditions are generally applicable rather than provider-specific.
General Conditions are distinct from significant-market-power conditions.
The current unofficial consolidated version took effect on 8 April 2026.
Condition B3 covers number portability when customers change provider.
Part C includes switching and porting protections for end users.
